title: Waste Segregation in the Operating Room
photoAlt: Waste Segregation in the Operating Room
description: This project aimed to improve waste segregation in the anesthesiology OR at St. Boniface Hospital and reduce unnecessary incineration of medical waste. Previously, a single pharmaceutical waste bin was used for mixed OR waste, which was then transported to Minnesota for high-carbon incineration. However, evidence suggests that most OR waste can instead be autoclaved or landfilled with lower environmental impact and cost. A new segregation system was therefore introduced with separate bins for sharps, pharmaceutical liquids, and general waste, supported by education sessions and ongoing staff coaching.

title: Northern Health Engagement tool
photoAlt: Northern Health Engagement tool
description: The initiative involved using the SE-QI Toolkit to support sustainability-focused quality improvement work within Northern Health, particularly in relation to clinical ideas such as reducing single-use materials, such as disposable patient gowns, and improving resource stewardship.
toolkitApplication: The Toolkit was used during meetings with clinical teams by inputting project ideas and guiding users through Steps 1–3 to explore sustainability opportunities and interpret outputs. It also helped identify relevant resources and demonstrated the Toolkit’s accessibility and practical utility for users unfamiliar with the field of planetary health.
toolkitAudienceUptake: The primary audience has been clinical teams and individuals initiating sustainability-related QI projects. Uptake has been early-stage and exploratory, with the Toolkit mainly used as an engagement and education tool.
mostValuableElements: Step 2 of the Toolkit was identified as the most valuable component due to its clear, structured presentation of resources that helped avoid unnecessary complexity. It enabled users to efficiently identify relevant pathways and supported quicker decision-making without requiring extensive independent research.
qiIntegrationComments: There is strong potential for the Toolkit to be integrated into routine QI work within Northern Health. Given limited capacity in current care models and few dedicated sustainability roles, the Toolkit could help provide structure and direction for teams pioneering people-oriented clinical sustainability initiatives.

title: Decrease of Personal Protective Device Failures
photoAlt: Decrease of Personal Protective Device Failures
description: An initiative at St. Paul’s Hospital aimed to reduce failures of personal protective devices caused by depleted batteries in the Psychiatric Assessment and Stabilization Unit. A structured inventory control and battery replacement process was introduced to improve equipment reliability, enhance staff and patient safety, and reduce disruptions to care.
cobenefit:
The Toolkit supports broader systems thinking by highlighting downstream effects, trade-offs, and co-benefits even in projects with mixed environmental implications.

title: Ontario Health's ONSQIN
photoAlt: Ontario Health's ONSQIN
description: An early-stage initiative involving exploration of the SE-QI Toolkit as a potential future resource to be introduced and disseminated to clinicians through Ontario Health’s Closing the Quality Gap campaign. toolkitAudienceUptake: The intended audience is ONSQIN members across approximately 55 hospitals in Ontario. Uptake is currently limited to pilot exploration, with initial use focused on testing feasibility and gathering insights to support potential future scaling.

title: Implementation of Rigid Sterilization Containers
photoAlt: Implementation of Rigid Sterilization Containers

title: Prompting Re-Assessment of Antidepressant Prescriptions
photoAlt: Prompting Re-Assessment of Antidepressant Prescriptions

description: This initiative aims to promote reassessment of antidepressant prescriptions in primary care for patients who have been on treatment for over one year, addressing potential inappropriate long-term prescribing and reflexive renewal by family physicians. title: Reducing the Climate Impact of Metered-Dose Inhalers
photoAlt: Reducing the Climate Impact of Metered-Dose Inhalers
description: This project was a collaboration between a primary care pharmacist and a family physician to reduce the environmental impact of inhaler prescribing in primary care. The initiative focused on optimizing respiratory care by assessing whether inhalers were needed, identifying opportunities for deprescribing when clinically appropriate, switching patients to lower-carbon dry powder inhalers, and providing education on inhaler disposal. Patients’ experiences with team-based care were also explored, including the role of sustainability considerations and the value of in-depth conversations in healthcare decision-making.
cobenefit: The Toolkit offers helpful reinforcement of existing knowledge and the reminder to consistently apply a sustainability lens when completing quality improvement work.

sustainabilityOpportunityComments.mitigationDecarbonization: Testing a more comprehensive and adaptable care approach through team-based care, involving collaboration between physicians, pharmacists, and patients. Educating patients on proper inhaler disposal and recycling practices.

title: Digitizing Lab Results in Nephrology Services
photoAlt: Digitizing Lab Results in Nephrology Services
description: An initiative in an outpatient renal clinic aimed to reduce paper waste by digitizing the receipt of community laboratory blood work results. The previous fax-based process generated approximately 70–120 pages per day, including cover sheets and duplicate reports that were routinely discarded.

title: Health Quality BC’s Quality Academy
photoAlt: Health Quality BC’s Quality Academy
description: Health Quality BC’s Quality Academy is a six-month professional development program that builds learners’ capability to lead quality and safety initiatives through formal instruction, mentorship, and an applied improvement project. The SE-QI Toolkit is now embedded in a dedicated session that explores how sustainability can be incorporated into quality improvement.
toolkitApplication: Learners are introduced to the SE-QI Toolkit and encouraged to apply it to their Quality Academy projects. They use the Toolkit to identify practical opportunities to incorporate sustainability considerations and relevant measures into the planning, implementation, and evaluation of their improvement work. This supports the program’s existing competencies related to measurement, systems thinking, and incorporating sustainability into quality improvement initiatives.
toolkitAudienceUptake:
The initiative is intended for Quality Academy learners from across British Columbia’s
health system, including clinical and non-clinical professionals from acute, primary,
community, long-term, residential, mental health, and other care settings who are
leading improvement projects.
In 2026, 16 Quality Academy participants identified how their QA projects aligned with
environmental sustainability in the Aligning Quality and Environmental Sustainability
session.
mostValuableElements: The most valuable components are the structured prompts that help teams identify sustainability opportunities, consider potential impacts across their projects, and select meaningful sustainability measures. The Toolkit’s practical and step-by-step format makes it adaptable to a wide range of Quality Academy projects and care settings.
qiIntegrationComments: The SE-QI Toolkit is now embedded within Health Quality BC’s Quality Academy as part of a dedicated session on integrating sustainability into quality improvement.

title: Healthcare Excellence Canada’s EXTRA Program
photoAlt: Healthcare Excellence Canada’s EXTRA Program
description: Healthcare Excellence Canada’s EXTRA program is a team-based, action-oriented leadership development program that supports healthcare leaders to advance quality, safety, and system transformation through applied improvement projects. The SE-QI Toolkit is now included within the EXTRA curriculum to strengthen participants’ capacity to integrate sustainability into their improvement work.
toolkitApplication: Two learning sessions are dedicated to sustainability during an in-person residency. The first introduces sustainable health systems and their connection to healthcare quality and improvement. The second introduces the SE-QI Toolkit and provides teams with dedicated time to apply it to their EXTRA improvement projects, identify relevant sustainability opportunities and impacts, and explore potential actions and measures.
toolkitAudienceUptake:
The target audience is EXTRA fellows participating in interdisciplinary teams from healthcare and social service organizations across Canada. Participants include healthcare leaders, people with lived experience, policy advisors and analysts, and quality and safety improvement leaders working on organizational or system-level improvement projects.
As the Toolkit’s inclusion in the curriculum is new, uptake will be assessed through participants’ engagement during the residency and its subsequent application within their EXTRA improvement projects.
mostValuableElements: The practical, step-by-step format helps teams translate broad sustainability concepts into concrete actions and relevant measures that can be incorporated into their existing improvement plans.
qiIntegrationComments:
The SE-QI Toolkit is now embedded within Healthcare Excellence Canada’s EXTRA curriculum through dedicated learning on sustainable health systems and the application of the Toolkit to participants’ improvement projects.
There is also potential to further integrate the Toolkit into other formal leadership-development, quality-improvement, coaching, and capacity-building programs offered by Healthcare Excellence Canada.

title: Pan-Canadian Network on Health System Response to Climate Change
photoAlt: Pan-Canadian Network on Health System Response to Climate Change
description:
The CASCADES Pan-Canadian Practice Network connects healthcare professionals and organizations across Canada to build capacity, exchange knowledge, and advance environmentally sustainable health systems. Within the Network, the SE-QI Working Group, co-chaired by Vancouver Coastal Health and Healthcare Excellence Canada, brings together representatives from participating organizations to advance the integration of sustainability into quality improvement practice.
The Working Group supports the mobilization, application, and continued improvement of the SE-QI Framework, Toolkit, and Spotlight, while fostering shared learning across organizations and helping strengthen the field of sustainability-embedded quality improvement in Canada.
toolkitApplication:
Participating organizations apply the SE-QI Toolkit to quality improvement projects, capacity-building initiatives, and/or educational programs within their respective settings. Working Group meetings provide opportunities for members to share how the Toolkit is being used, discuss implementation experiences and challenges, and identify opportunities to strengthen its content and usability.
Members are also supported to embed the Toolkit within existing organizational structures and programs and to develop submissions for the SE-QI Spotlight. These examples help mobilize learning within the Network and more broadly across the Canadian health system.
toolkitAudienceUptake:
The initiative is intended for healthcare professionals, quality improvement leaders, sustainability and planetary health leaders, educators, and organizational partners from organizations participating in the Pan-Canadian Practice Network who are seeking to integrate sustainability into improvement initiatives. 
As of July 2026, the SE-QI Working Group includes 19 participants representing 12 local or regional healthcare organizations, one pan-Canadian organization, and four provinces. Participating organizations are at different stages of implementation: some have applied the Toolkit to specific improvement projects, while others are exploring opportunities to embed it within formal QI programs, educational initiatives, and organizational processes.
mostValuableElements: The identification of key SE-QI principles and the Toolkit’s structured, guided approach are particularly valuable, as they help teams make clear connections between quality improvement and sustainability. The inclusion of practical calculators within the Toolkit’s resources is also valuable, as it makes it easier for teams to quantify relevant environmental and other sustainability impacts.
qiIntegrationComments: The SE-QI Toolkit is already embedded at the centre of the Working Group’s activities, providing participating organizations with a shared foundation, common language, and practical tools to integrate sustainability into quality improvement.

title: IH Physician Quality Improvement Program
photoAlt: IH Physician Quality Improvement Program
description:
The Interior Health (IH) Physician Quality Improvement (PQI) Level 3 Advanced Cohort Training is a 10-month applied learning program that supports physicians to develop quality improvement skills and lead improvement projects within their clinical settings. Planetary health content has been included in the curriculum since 2023, and the SE-QI Toolkit has been formally embedded since 2024 to support participants in integrating sustainability into their improvement work. 

In partnership, the Interior Health and Vancouver Coastal Health (VCH) PQI programs inspired the Toolkit, served as early testing environments, and helped inform its formal development.
toolkitApplication:
A dedicated planetary health session is included in the Level 3 curriculum. The session introduces the relationship between planetary health and quality improvement, provides an overview of the SE-QI Toolkit, and invites teams to apply it to their own projects. 
Participants can also access support from the IH Planetary Health team to identify sustainability opportunities, select relevant measures, and further integrate the Toolkit into their projects. IH first introduced a dedicated session on the intersection of planetary health and quality improvement in 2023.
toolkitAudienceUptake:
The initiative is intended for physicians participating in the IH PQI Level 3 Advanced Cohort Training who are leading applied quality improvement projects across a range of clinical settings. 
Planetary health content has been delivered to Level 3 cohorts since 2023, with the SE-QI Toolkit formally embedded since 2024.  
Participants are introduced to the Toolkit during the dedicated planetary health session and encouraged to apply it to their projects, with additional support available from the Planetary Health team.
mostValuableElements: The Toolkit’s guided structure and practical resources, including calculators, are particularly valuable in helping teams identify, assess, and quantify relevant sustainability impacts within their projects. The principles introduced in Step 1 also provide a shared language for discussing the links between quality improvement and sustainability, while encouraging consideration of both upstream and downstream impacts beyond more commonly recognized activities such as recycling.
qiIntegrationComments: The SE-QI Toolkit is already formally embedded within the IH PQI Level 3 curriculum and provides participants with a consistent approach for incorporating sustainability into their improvement projects.

title: VCH/PHC Physician Quality Improvement Program
photoAlt: VCH/PHC Physician Quality Improvement Program
description: In partnership, the Interior Health and Vancouver Coastal Health Physician Quality Improvement (PQI) programs inspired the Toolkit, served as early testing environments, and helped inform its formal development.

Participants can also access support from the VCH Planetary Health team to identify sustainability opportunities, select relevant measures, and further integrate the Toolkit into their projects. title: Coastal Complex Outpatient Antimicrobial Therapy (COpAT) Program - LGH Pilot
photoAlt: Coastal Complex Outpatient Antimicrobial Therapy (COpAT) Program - LGH Pilot
description: Lions Gate Hospital (LGH) will launch the Complex Outpatient Antimicrobial Therapy (COpAT) program, which integrates the existing Community IV Program (CPIV) with a new Community PO (oral) Program pilot (CPOP). Led by Infectious Disease specialists and supported by Medical Day Care staff and a clinical pharmacist, COpAT will provide specialist oversight and routine monitoring for eligible North Shore residents receiving either IV or evidence-supported oral antimicrobial therapy for complex infections.
cobenefit: The carbon footprint estimation examples and resources were particularly useful, making the process of capturing a project's environmental impact feel less intimidating and more achievable through high-level estimates based on the provided references and calculations.

sustainabilityOpportunityComments.prevention: CPOP provides a non-invasive, needle-free experience that eliminates risks associated with vascular access (e.g., infections, thrombosis) and improves daily autonomy.
sustainabilityOpportunityComments.climateResilienceAdaptation: CPOP optimizes clinic capacity and resource allocation by reducing the need for PICC line insertions, maintenance appointments, and sterile compounding workload. This further provides significant cost savings on PICC supplies and IV medications. It further eliminates patient visits to ambulatory clinic for line-care.

environmental: Environmental impact data will be collected using a simulation-based approach, with a UBC Pharmacy Directed Studies student weighing clean plastic compounding and oral packaging supplies associated with commonly prescribed antimicrobials in the Community IV (CIVP) and Community PO (CPOP) streams. Pending approval, materials used for PICC insertion and clinic care will also be measured. Plastic waste mass will then be scaled to program volumes to estimate the potential waste reduction associated with oral therapy.
activity: Estimation of number of trips to ambulatory clinics eliminated by placing a patient in CPOP instead of CIVP.

domainsOfQuality.name: Efficiency
domainsOfQuality.explanation: Emerging medical evidence now supports oral (PO) therapy for many complex infections traditionally treated with IV. The CPOP pilot provides the formal framework clinicians need to apply this evidence, ensuring patients receive the same specialist oversight and monitoring as those on IV therapy.

domainsOfQuality.name: Safety
domainsOfQuality.explanation: CPOP provides a non-invasive, needle-free treatment option that eliminates risks associated with vascular access, including catheter-related infections and thrombosis.

domainsOfQuality.name: Timeliness
domainsOfQuality.explanation: Arranging CIVP therapy can take several days, potentially prolonging hospital length of stay. For eligible patients, CPOP may enable earlier transition to outpatient treatment, reducing hospital length of stay and associated risks of hospitalization.

domainsOfQuality.name: Patient-Centredness / Respect
domainsOfQuality.explanation: For those patients who prefer to receive treatment orally, the CPOP program provides the opportunity to match the patient's preference should they be deemed eligible.

title: Fraser Health Engagement Tool
photoAlt: Fraser Health Engagement Tool
description: Fraser Health is building QI teams’ awareness of the SE-QI Toolkit and how the toolkit can support further incorporation of sustainability into quality improvement. Promotion includes presentations, newsletter articles, one-to-one work with project leads, and informal advocacy.
toolkitApplication: The SE-QI Toolkit has been tested with a number of Choosing Wisely and waste reduction projects to explore its practical application, including the use of its reporting resources. Integration into a formal PPH QI program has been suggested, with details still being explored. mostValuableElements: The activity metrics and outcome resources were identified as particularly valuable. These tools and verified sources help teams identify and document outcomes of their efforts related to environmental sustainability.
qiIntegrationComments: Fraser Health hopes to embed the SE-QI Toolkit within its broader QI resources, with the longer-term goal of making it available for and used by all QI projects. This would support more consistent integration of sustainability considerations across QI activities.

title: Reusable Silicone Tourniquet for Venous Access: A Sustainability Initiative
photoAlt: Reusable Silicone Tourniquet for Venous Access: A Sustainability Initiative
description: The silicone reusable tourniquet project is a clinical study focused on replacing single‑use tourniquets with reusable silicone tourniquets in the IWK Health Pediatric Emergency Department, phlebotomy and Pediatric Perioperative Team. The project examines whether reusable tourniquets can be safely and effectively integrated into everyday care while reducing waste and improving environmental performance. It focuses on feasibility, safety, acceptability and sustainability impact.

title: Intravenous to Oral Antimicrobial Switch: A Win for Patients and the Planet
photoAlt: Intravenous to Oral Antimicrobial Switch: A Win for Patients and the Planet
description:
Health care accounts for 4.6% of Canada's greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, 25% of which comes from medications. Antimicrobials with high bioavailability offer no additional benefit when given intravenously, except when oral (PO) administration is not feasible. Intravenous (IV) formulations have a higher carbon footprint than their PO counterparts. IV-to-PO switch strategies benefit patients and the health care system by reducing line-related adverse events, nursing time, length of hospital stay, and costs and can also reduce carbon emissions.

Our primary objective was to quantify IV use of bioequivalent antimicrobials when PO administration is feasible. Secondary objectives were to determine GHG emissions and antimicrobial costs associated with unnecessary IV use of bioequivalent antimicrobials.

We performed a retrospective, cross-sectional study of hospitalized adults who received IV azithromycin, ciprofloxacin, clindamycin, cotrimoxazole, fluconazole, levofloxacin, linezolid, metronidazole, moxifloxacin, or voriconazole at Vancouver General Hospital on five dates. We determined the proportion of patients receiving these antimicrobials who met criteria for PO administration. We collaborated with the UBC Clean Energy Research Centre and applied a life cycle assessment (LCA) to assess the GHG emissions of the antimicrobial drug delivery systems using OpenLCA with the Ecoinvent database. Using these data, we calculated the GHG emissions and costs associated with unnecessary IV use.
cobenefit: The SE-QI Toolkit helped inspire our team to apply a planetary health lens to quality improvement.

environmental: We performed a consequential LCA of two drug delivery systems (IV versus PO), which focused on the materials used for drug delivery and excluded the manufacturing of the drugs since we assumed they would be made under identical conditions. The amount of drug used was similar between the IV and PO formulations for bioequivalent antimicrobials; therefore, we focused only on the waste materials for drug preparation, distribution, and administration.

IV systems showed a much higher carbon footprint (785.4 to 2,088.5 gCO2-eq/FU) compared to the PO system, attributed to the higher amount of materials used in preparing and administering each dose of the drug. The major contributor was material production, while the transportation stage had minor impacts on overall carbon footprints. For nonhazardous drugs, landfill disposal resulted in a smaller amount of GHG emissions, as most of these materials were recalcitrant to decompose. However, the incineration of materials contaminated by hazardous drugs (fluconazole and voriconazole) added significant emissions even with energy recovery for power generation. The emissions related to drug packaging varied significantly depending on the type of packaging materials. The systems that required a compounding pharmacy process demonstrated much higher GHG emissions than those systems using premixed bags. Using the GHG estimates, switching eligible patients from IV to PO administration was associated with potential savings of approximately 80,000 gCO2-eq over the five audit dates. Extrapolated to one year, this corresponds to a reduction of 5.78 tonnes CO2-eq (±25% sensitivity range 4.33–7.22 tonnes CO2-eq). On average, the GHG savings per eligible patient per day were 1,014 gCO2-eq (±25% sensitivity range 761–1,268 gCO2-eq), equivalent to driving a gas-powered car approximately 5 km.
activity: In total, 128 patients were identified. Seventy-eight (61%) met IV-to-PO switch criteria on the audit dates. Most eligible patients were admitted to general surgery, internal medicine, or critical care. The antimicrobial with the highest IV-to-PO switch eligibility was metronidazole (51%), most often prescribed for intra-abdominal infections. Over the five study dates, potential GHG savings were about 80,000 gCO2-eq. Potential annual cost savings were about $59,000.

title: Embedding Sustainability Principles and Tools into an Interdisciplinary QI Fellowship
photoAlt: Embedding Sustainability Principles and Tools into an Interdisciplinary QI Fellowship
description:
The Barrett Centre for Quality Improvement (BCQI) was formed in 2025 through a generous donation from the Barrett Family Foundation. The BCQI’s vision is to embed QI initiatives throughout the St. Joseph’s site by enhancing a culture of continuous learning, encouraging innovation, and empowering people through capacity building to collaborate on solutions that improve outcomes, patient experience, and staff well-being. The cornerstone of the BCQI is the QI Fellowship Program, an interdisciplinary project-based program rooted in Lean Six Sigma and Model for Improvement methodologies. 

In 2026, as part of the fellowship curriculum, the team trialed incorporating a dedicated session on Embedding Sustainability into QI. In partnership with Nicole Simms, Training and Education Lead of CASCADES, fellows learned about sustainability & climate resilience as a health system priority, the SE-QI Framework, and how to mobilize the SE-QI toolkit, especially for fellowship projects where sustainability may be a co-benefit.

By integrating established sustainability tools and principles into the QI fellowship, the fellows are learning how quality improvement can simultaneously advance patient care and environmental stewardship.
toolkitApplication: The toolkit was introduced as a tool for our QI fellows to use in their projects as well as explore opportunities for application in their daily practice throughout the healthcare centre, where sustainability may be a co-benefit.
toolkitAudienceUptake: In progress, information shared with our cohort of 38 fellows
mostValuableElements:
After the session, most respondents (83.3%, n=12) agreed or strongly agreed that they could identify opportunities to incorporate environmental sustainability into QI work. When asked how the fellows plan to apply the knowledge and tools to their work, fellows noted: 

“Moving forward I will use this information to predict future outcome utilizing data to reduce waste” 

“Incorporate sustainability principles (directly or indirectly) to our QI initiatives.”
